correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed at the level of the full parameterized Rankine--Hugoniot map. The unknown vector has dimension \(n^2\): \(n-1\) intermediate states plus \(n\) speeds. At a strict Lax zero, every right-state block \(A_k=DF(u^{(k)})-s_kI\) is invertible because \(s_k\) lies strictly between characteristic speeds at the right state. In the total derivative with endpoint parameters included, the columns for \(u^{(1)},\ldots,u^{(n-1)},u_r\) form a block lower-triangular square matrix with diagonal \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\); hence the total map is a submersion on the admissible open locus. The finite-dimensional parametric transversality theorem therefore gives regularity of every admissible zero for almost every endpoint pair, and since the fixed-endpoint derivative is square it is invertible. The Banach-space implicit function theorem then gives a unique nearby chain under small endpoint and \(C^2\)-flux perturbations; strict hyperbolicity, Lax inequalities, nonzero jumps and speed order persist by openness. The theorem is conditional on existence and makes no unsupported existence claim.

value.rationale: The current general structural-stability theorem pays for mixed shock/rarefaction patterns with substantial global regularity assumptions. Showing that the physically important all-shock pattern needs only strict hyperbolicity isolates exactly which hypotheses belong to rarefaction/global-Hugoniot geometry and yields a cleaner arbitrary-dimensional robustness theorem. This is a motivated structural strengthening, not a routine special case, because the conclusion holds for a larger flux class despite the narrower wave pattern.
residual_risks: The theorem does not treat rarefactions, contacts, composite or undercompressive waves, and it is conditional on an admissible all-shock chain existing.
